topic_ko: 공원에서의 우연한 만남 — Sally와 바이올린 노부인
_note: story 순서(43-45) FULL set. narrative 지문이므로 order/insert/grammar/vocab/summary/writing만 작성. 유형마다 passage를 다르게 paraphrase. grammar/vocab의 밑줄 어구는 해당 passage 문장에 글자 그대로 존재.

order.given: Every afternoon, Sally would pass through the park on her way home from school, always wearing her headphones. One day, she heard unfamiliar, rough music drifting through the trees and took off her headphones to listen.

blocks.A: She followed the sound and found an elderly woman sitting on a bench, playing the violin with warmth despite not being perfect. Curious and drawn in, Sally walked over to her.
blocks.B: The following afternoon, they met at the same bench. The old woman handed Sally the violin and announced it was time for her first proper lesson. She guided Sally on how to hold her fingers on the strings, and after an hour, Sally had picked up the basics. As she walked home, the simple, unpolished melody echoed in her mind.
blocks.C: After listening to the woman finish her piece, Sally learned she had only started playing the year before. When the woman asked if Sally played any instrument, Sally recalled her older sister once telling her she had no musical gift. The old woman smiled, placed the violin in Sally's hands, and said, "You don't need talent to enjoy it." Sally tried playing — the sound was rough — but the woman just encouraged her: "That's how it begins. Come back tomorrow."

order.explanation_ko: 주어진 글에서 Sally가 공원에서 낯선 음악을 따라가는 장면 → (A)에서 벤치의 노부인에게 다가감 → (C)에서 첫 대화: 노부인의 배경, Sally의 과거(Beatrice), 첫 연주 시도, '내일 오라'는 권유 → (B)에서 다음 날 첫 정식 레슨과 마무리로 이어짐. (A)-(C)-(B)가 정답.
order.distractor_ko: (B)의 'the following afternoon'은 전날 만남이 있어야 성립하므로 (A)와 (C) 뒤에 와야 한다. (C)에서 'Come back tomorrow'가 (B)의 다음 날을 직접 연결한다.

insert.insert_sentence: Feeling brave, Sally accepted the instrument and tried playing.

passage_marked.text: The old woman asked Sally if she played any instruments.
Suddenly, Sally remembered learning the recorder from her older sister Beatrice when she was a girl.
Sally looked back to the old woman sadly and told (c)her the story.
The old woman winked, handed the violin to Sally, and said, "You don't need talent to enjoy playing."
But the old woman just smiled and said, "That's how it begins.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장 'Feeling brave, Sally accepted the instrument and tried playing'은 노부인이 '재능 없어도 즐길 수 있다'며 바이올린을 건네준 직후(④ 뒤)에 와야 자연스럽다. Sally가 용기를 내어 악기를 받아든 것이 '소리가 거칠었다'는 ⑤ 앞의 내용으로 이어진다.
insert.distractor_ko: ①②③은 아직 Sally가 Beatrice 이야기를 하거나 슬퍼하는 단계라 악기를 받을 상황이 아니다. ⑤ 뒤는 이미 연주를 마친 이후의 반응 단계이다.

passage: Every day after school, Sally walked home through the park.
She liked listening to music in her headphones and looking at the trees on her way home.
One day, while she was changing songs, she heard strange, unpolished music.
She took off her headphones and followed the music through the park.
She saw a kind-looking old woman sitting on a small bench and to play the violin.
While (a)her music wasn't perfect, there was something warm and welcoming about it.
Sally laughed and replied, "Oh sorry, I was just passing by."
(e)She turned to continue walking home, but decided to stop for a bit and listen.

underlines.text: listening to music in her headphones

grammar.explanation_ko: ④ 지각동사 saw의 목적격 보어 자리에는 현재분사 또는 동사원형이 와야 한다. to play(to부정사)는 이 자리에 올 수 없다 → playing the violin 으로 고쳐야 한다.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①liked + -ing(동명사) 올바름, ②while + 과거진행 올바름, ③단순과거 followed 올바름, ⑤decided to stop(decide + to V) 올바름.

passage: Every day after school, Sally walked home through the park.
One day, while she was changing songs, she heard strange, unpolished music.
She took off her headphones and followed the music through the park.
She saw a kind-looking old woman sitting on a small bench and playing the violin.
While her music wasn't perfect, there was something warm and welcoming about it.
Sally laughed and replied, "Oh sorry, I was just passing by."
After the woman's music finished, Sally asked her when she had started playing the violin.
Beatrice had said, "You just have no musical talent."
The old woman winked, handed the violin to Sally, and said, "You don't need talent to enjoy playing."
Feeling brave, Sally accepted the instrument and tried playing.
The sound was smooth, and she felt embarrassed.
Sally promised to meet her every day and started walking home.
As she walked, simple, unpolished music was playing in her mind.
vocab.explanation_ko: ④ Sally가 처음 바이올린을 연주하자 창피함을 느꼈으므로 소리는 'rough(거친)'이어야 한다. smooth(부드러운)는 감정 반응(embarrassed)과 모순이다 → rough로 고쳐야 한다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①unpolished(다듬어지지 않은, 거친) — 처음부터 노부인의 음악을 묘사하는 어휘로 올바름. ②welcoming(포근한) — Sally를 끌어당긴 음악의 특성으로 올바름. ③accepted(받아들였다) — 용기를 내어 악기를 수락한 것으로 올바름. ⑤unpolished — 마지막 문장에서 Sally 마음속 음악 묘사로 올바름.

passage: Every day after school, Sally passed through the park wearing headphones, but one day she removed them when she heard strange, rough music.
She found an elderly woman on a bench playing the violin imperfectly yet warmly.
After listening, Sally learned the woman had only started playing the year before — always having wanted to learn.
When the woman asked if Sally played any instrument, Sally recalled her sister Beatrice's words: that she had no musical talent.
The old woman dismissed this and handed Sally the violin, saying talent was not needed to enjoy playing.
Sally tried, made rough sounds, felt embarrassed, but the woman smiled and invited her to return the next day.
The following day, the woman gave Sally her first real lesson on finger placement.
Walking home after an hour of practice, Sally found the simple, unpolished melody playing quietly in her mind.
summary.summary_template: Sally's chance encounter with an elderly woman in the park inspires her to __(A)__ the violin despite her fear that she has no __(B)__, showing that the desire to learn matters more than innate ability.
summary.explanation_ko: Sally가 Beatrice에게 'no musical talent'라는 말을 들었음에도 노부인의 권유와 격려로 바이올린을 (A)learn(배우기) 시작하는 내용. 극복 대상은 (B)talent(재능) 없다는 두려움이다. ①이 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: ②abandon(포기)과 ⑤avoid(피하다)는 Sally의 실제 행동과 반대. ③teach(가르치다)는 Sally의 역할이 아님. ④time(시간)은 이야기에서 장애 요소가 아니다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그녀는 친절해 보이는 한 노부인이 작은 벤치에 앉아 바이올린을 켜고 있는 것을 보았다.
writing.answer: She saw a kind-looking old woman sitting on a small bench and playing the violin.
writing.explanation_ko: 지각동사 saw + 목적어(a kind-looking old woman) + 현재분사(sitting ... and playing) 구문.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 용기를 내어, Sally는 악기를 받아들고 연주를 시도했다.
writing.answer: Feeling brave, Sally accepted the instrument and tried playing.
writing.explanation_ko: 분사구문 Feeling brave + 주어 Sally + accepted + and tried playing(try + -ing = 실제로 해보다).

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 갑자기, Sally는 어렸을 때 언니 Beatrice에게 리코더를 배웠던 것이 기억났다.
conditions: when she was a girl을 포함할 것
writing.answer: Suddenly, Sally remembered learning the recorder from her older sister Beatrice when she was a girl.
writing.explanation_ko: remember + -ing(과거 사실을 기억하다), from her older sister Beatrice(~에게서), when she was a girl(어렸을 때).

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: The old woman winked, handed the violin to Sally, and said, "You don't need talent to enjoy playing."
writing.answer: 노부인은 눈을 찡긋하며, Sally에게 바이올린을 건네고, "연주를 즐기는 데 재능은 필요 없어요"라고 말했다.
writing.explanation_ko: winked(눈을 찡긋했다), handed A to B(B에게 A를 건네다), don't need + 명사 + to V(~하는 데 ~이 필요 없다).

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: As she walked, simple, unpolished music was playing in her mind.
writing.answer: 걸어가면서, 단순하고 다듬어지지 않은 음악이 그녀의 마음속에서 흘렀다.
writing.explanation_ko: as + 절(~하면서, 동시동작), unpolished(다듬어지지 않은), was playing in her mind(마음속에서 흘렀다).

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
writing.summary: Sally began to (A)___________ the violin after being encouraged by an elderly woman who told her that (B)___________ was not necessary to enjoy playing music.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) Sally는 바이올린을 배우기 시작했다 — learn. (B) 노부인이 한 말 'You don't need talent to enjoy playing' → talent.
